name: The window does one task
sees: The product's own window, large and held on screen, acts out the one thing the page promises the visitor (the invoice sent, the booking made, the report shared): a field fills, the list answers, the cursor presses the action, and the result lands as a change in the layout. The task is the promise kept, in the product's real labels and figures, never a tour of the interface for its own sake. The section's heading states that promise; the window proves it.
beats: a field fills (typed at 40-60 ms a letter) → the list filters or the panel opens → the cursor presses the action (a 2px press) → the result the visitor wanted lands as a change in the layout (the row moves to Done by FLIP, the count ticks); each beat about half a screen of scroll
phone: Held as on desktop, the window nearly the full width: the field and the list under it, the same four beats.

name: The agent works beside its result
sees: One line of request, the agent's own status line under it, and the work it changes beside it, held on screen while it works. The request is the job the page promises to take off the visitor's hands, each status names what the agent does to the rows in view, and it ends on the result the visitor wanted (the mistake found, the reply drafted, the books balanced), never on a bare "Done".
beats: the request types in one line → the agent's line reads "Reading 412 entries" as the rows settle → "Checking against the bank feed" as an accent frame lands on one cell → "Fixed: a duplicate refund" as that cell rolls to the right figure and the total re-counts; each beat about half a screen of scroll
phone: Held as on desktop: the request and the status line over the table, cropped to the rows that change, nearly the full width.

name: The board moves its own card
sees: A board of the visitor's own items in three or four columns, held on screen while one of them moves. The move acts out the page's promise (an order packed the day it lands, a ticket closed before lunch, an old note brought back beside the draft): the card that moves is the one the promise is about, and the column it reaches is the result the visitor wants. Never a card shuffled between columns for show; when the product's promise is not a move from one state to the next, this replay is the wrong one (draw.mjs --redraw replay).
beats: a new item drops in at the top of column one (its count ticks) → the cursor lifts the item the promise is about (accent left edge, 2° tilt) → carries it to the column that means the promise kept, which opens a slot while the old one closes → both counts tick and its status word changes; each beat about half a screen of scroll
phone: Held as on desktop: two columns of the board, the move between them, nearly the full width.

name: Teammates take turns
sees: One shared object (a document, a plan, a design) and two or three named cursors, each making one change in turn, held on screen while they work. The object ends finished, which is what the page promises a team (the plan agreed without a meeting, the review done in a day); each change is a real part of that object, never a cursor wandering for show.
beats: cursor "Ines" moves one block two places down (a note line under her name tag) → cursor "Agent" fills a missing figure → cursor "Tom" adds one comment → the object rests finished; each beat about half a screen of scroll
phone: Held as on desktop: the object cropped to the blocks that change, the cursors' name tags kept, nearly the full width.

name: Edit the source, the output rebuilds
sees: The source (a query, a formula, a config) beside the output it makes, held on screen while one value changes. The page's promise is that one edit is enough, so one value changes in the source and the same marks in the output travel to their new places: the answer the visitor was after, rebuilt in front of them.
beats: the source line retypes one value ("last 30 days" → "last 90 days") → the output's marks travel to their new places (the same elements, FLIP) → the read-out re-counts ("1,240 rows → 3,912 rows · 0.4 s"); each beat about half a screen of scroll
phone: Held as on desktop: the source line over the output, stacked, nearly the full width.

name: A frame tours the live screen
sees: The whole screen of the product with three feature lines beside it, held on screen while an accent frame steps from region to region. Each stop is one thing the product does for the visitor (counts the stock, reorders what runs low, keeps the total right), a value changes there, and the matching line turns to full ink. The lines stand beside the regions they name, so neither column is left empty.
beats: a 2px accent frame steps (not glides) to region one and one value changes (38 → 41) → to region two, a status flips (Low → Ordered) → to region three, the total recalculates; the matching feature line beside the window turns full ink at each stop, and the lines are buttons that scroll to their stop; each stop about half a screen of scroll
phone: Held as on desktop: the three lines in a row above the window, nearly the full width; the frame steps the same way.
